✅ **Prompt Updated**: Showcase Asset Sheet (showcase_asset_sheet)

Updated prompt: showcase_asset_sheet

📜 **Version 2** saved (use `action:"history"` to view)

**Changes**: +20 additions, -1 deletions

```diff
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_asset_sheet/user-message.md
+++ b/development/showcase_asset_sheet/user-message.md
@@ -4,4 +4,23 @@
 
 Read `v3/creative-spec.md` (D65–D68: drawings come from the image model, never from coordinates; the plate must cut into movable layers), `v3/script.md` (the asset's job) and `v3/rubric.md` (C1–C19). For each muse direction (3 or more) generate one sheet through the `imagegen` tool (`tool:imagegen`), never by hand: `references` are the absolute paths of the board cards the direction cites (`v3/references/board.json` → file under `v3/references/`), the `prompt` names which reference supplies which property, asks for a pure black field, five flat colors, pale contour one step lighter, identity pigments by hex, and a parts layout (full figure plus separated head, torso, hands, hair on the same sheet) so the cutout step can rig it; `out` is `media/showcase/out/<asset>-gen-<NN>-<direction>.png`. Lay the generations into the `AssetSheet` composition as images with their labels (borrows by card id, between by cast property) and render one still at frame 0 under {{files}}. Keep every generation's receipt (prompt, referenced_image_paths, source, sha256) in the step output. Do not pick; the owner picks from the still. A generation that is not cuttable into layers (merged parts, gradients across parts, text) is marked REJECTED on the sheet and regenerated once.
 
-Return: Variants (id, title, borrows, between, generation receipt); Sheet Path; What Was Held Constant; Rejected Generations; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file
+File the picks as proposals (D94, D95). For each direction, write one proposal file `v3/proposals/pNNN-<slug>.json` of kind `inspiration`: NNN is the highest existing proposal number plus one (list `v3/proposals/` first; ids are never reused), `<slug>` is the asset and direction in at most five kebab-case words. One file per direction, in this shape and no other:
+```json
+{
+  "id": "pNNN",
+  "kind": "inspiration",
+  "from": "chain:showcase_asset_muse#<run>",
+  "date": "<today, YYYY-MM-DD>",
+  "anchor": {"beat": "<beat id from v3/timeline.json>"},
+  "title": "<asset>: <direction title>",
+  "text": "<what this direction borrows and from which reference (card id and facet), and the cast property it sits between>",
+  "references": ["<board card id or owner-library pick id the direction borrows from>"],
+  "before": {"note": "<how the asset is drawn now, or 'not yet drawn'>"},
+  "after": {"frames": ["media/showcase/out/<asset>-gen-<NN>-<direction>.png"], "note": "<what the sheet shows>"},
+  "status": "open",
+  "ruling": null
+}
+```
+The anchor beat is the first beat the asset appears in, read from the brief (the asset argument names its job in the script) against `v3/script.md` and the beat ids in `v3/timeline.json`; give the beat id only, no frame. `references` lists only ids that exist on the board (`v3/references/board.json`) or in the owner picks (`v3/references/owner/picks.json`), because the bible flags an id it cannot resolve. `after.frames` names the sheet image for that direction so the page shows it at the beat. Leave `status` open and `ruling` null: the owner's pick is a ruling, written by the page, and a REJECTED generation gets no proposal. After the files are written, run `npm run bible` in the production root and quote its pass line, or on a refusal quote the refused line without editing the bible, the probe or a proposal to get past it.
+
+Return: Variants (id, title, borrows, between, generation receipt); Sheet Path; Proposals Filed (id, direction, anchor beat); What Was Held Constant; Rejected Generations; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file

```
